title: Hear No Evil: Detecting Gradient Leakage by Malicious Servers in Federated Learning
abstract: arXiv:2506.20651v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recent work has shown that gradient updates in federated learning (FL) can unintentionally reveal sensitive information about a client's local data. This risk becomes significantly greater when a malicious server manipulates the global model to provoke information-rich updates from clients. In this paper, we adopt a defender's perspective to provide the first comprehensive analysis of malicious gradient leakage attacks and the model manipulation techniques that enable them. Our investigation reveals a core trade-off: these attacks cannot be both highly effective in reconstructing private data and sufficiently stealthy to evade detection -- especially in realistic FL settings that incorporate common normalization techniques and federated averaging.   Building on this insight, we argue that malicious gradient leakage attacks, while theoretically concerning, are inherently limited in practice and often detectable through basic monitoring.

translated_title: 非礼勿听：检测联邦学习中恶意服务器导致的梯度泄露
translated_abstract: 近期的研究表明，联邦学习（FL）中的梯度更新可能会在无意中泄露有关客户端本地数据的敏感信息。当恶意服务器操纵全局模型以诱发客户端产生信息丰富的更新时，这种风险会显著增大。在本文中，我们采用防御者的视角，首次对恶意梯度泄露攻击及其所依赖的模型操纵技术进行了全面分析。我们的研究揭示了一个核心权衡：这些攻击无法同时在重建私有数据方面高度有效，又足够隐蔽以逃避检测——尤其是在融合了常见归一化技术和联邦平均的现实联邦学习设置中。基于这一洞见，我们认为恶意梯度泄露攻击虽然在理论上令人担忧，但在实践中存在固有限制，并且通常可以通过基本的监控手段检测出来。
tldr: 本文首次从防御者视角对联邦学习中恶意服务器的梯度泄露攻击进行全面分析，揭示了此类攻击在数据重建效果与隐蔽性之间存在根本性权衡，证明其在现实场景中固有受限且可通过基本监控检测。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first defender-perspective comprehensive analysis of malicious gradient leakage attacks in federated learning, revealing a fundamental trade-off between data reconstruction effectiveness and stealthiness, and demonstrating that such attacks are inherently limited in realistic settings and detectable through basic monitoring.
